newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico faces lengthy extradition battle for lawman.
newsitem.headline: Mexico faces lengthy extradition battle for lawman.

text.p: Mexican authorities may face a long battle to have a former prosecutor extradited from Spain to face charges of rigging evidence in the investigation of a leading politician's murder.
Pablo Chapa, who has been on the run since February, was arrested as he left a Madrid restaurant on Friday and jailed pending extradition proceedings.
The Mexican government newspaper El Nacional, however, said on Sunday that the process of getting Chapa extradited back to Mexico could take up to 18 months.

President Ernesto Zedillo's government, facing mid-term elections on July 6, would like to get him back sooner, allowing it to show progress in cracking a case that has badly damaged the image of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
"If Spanish authorities find that Chapa entered Spain illegally -- using false paperwork or jumping the border -- he will be expelled in a matter of days," a Mexican government source told Reuters.

Spanish newspaper Diario 16 said the 46-year-old Chapa fled Mexico hidden in the trunk of a car. The escape could have been through the United States, Guatemala or Belize, Mexico's three neighbouring nations.
Mexican newspapers said Chapa may have used a false passport to enter Spain. El Financiero claimed Chapa will try to avoid extradition by applying for Spanish citizenship.

Chapa fled Mexico after authorities accused him of rigging evidence while acting as the special prosector in a case against the brother of former president Carlos Salinas, Raul, who is in jail on corruption charges.

Charges were brought against Chapa in February after the discovery of a skeleton on the grounds of Raul Salinas' ranch on the outskirts of Mexico City. Chapa ordered Raul Salinas' arrest in February 1995 on charges of masterminding the murder of PRI secretary-general Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
The former lawman led the public to believe that the body was that of a missing congressman wanted on charges of helping Raul Salinas murder the politician.

Special investigators and forensic experts, however, found it was the skeleton of a relative of a psychic helping Chapa in the investigation. Chapa allegedly paid her to have a dead relative dug up and planted in Salinas' ranch.
Chapa was fired from his post in the Attorney General's Office last December. He went into hiding in February.
Opposition parties think the case will become a political football in the run-up to the crucial July 6 elections where the control of Congress and several key governorships are at stake.
If Chapa were extradited quickly, the PRI could not only show progress in solving the crime but also use the case to attack the opposition.

Former Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia, a member of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), was Chapa's boss. The PRI has capitalised on the bungled Salinas case under Lozano to discredit the PAN, one of two leading opposition parties.
"Justice should not be subject to campaign calendars. I hope the arrest of Chapa Bezanilla has nothing to do with the fact we are in the middle of an election," PAN congresswoman Cecilia Romero said.
